headline: High: shared filesystem and broad tool/network access create prompt-injection, leakage, and write-conflict risks; Open WebUI’s persistent sessions amplify cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline ingests workspace files, runs browsers, and uses MCP with no default isolation; open-webui supports MCP/plugins and persistent sessions. If Cline writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or MCP outputs, open-webui can parse it as instructions. The shared filesystem bridge makes this a direct pairwise injection path.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or mounted volume, injected instructions can cross from Cline to open-webui.
IF open-webui consumes file or MCP content as trusted prompt material, attacker text can steer downstream actions.
mitigations: Separate the agents onto different workspaces.
Disable MCP on one side during shared tasks.
Add a manual review step for any file passed between agents.
Use read-only mounts for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline reads and writes workspace files and handles model-provider API keys; open-webui can access local/mounted files, persistent memory, and API keys. With shared filesystem state and broad egress, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Cline into open-webui outputs or third-party APIs without strong isolation.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace or mounted data volume, files touched by Cline can be read by open-webui.
IF open-webui forwards those files to external APIs, the leakage leaves the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared folders.
Use separate API keys per agent.
Mount shared data read-only for open-webui.
Turn off external connectors for sensitive sessions.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline can modify git state and write the filesystem; open-webui can access local files and mounted volumes, and both support multiple instances. Because Cline’s shared state is via filesystem and open-webui uses persistent shared sessions, concurrent writes to the same repo or volume can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. No locking is documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository, concurrent edits can conflict.
IF either agent commits or rewrites files without external locking, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Pause one agent before the other writes.
Use git worktrees per agent.
Add a manual merge checkpoint before commits.
requires-engineering: implement file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can produce browser-derived content and file edits; open-webui can persist memory and route outputs through tools or APIs. The pair creates a plausible chain where open-webui treats Cline’s output as authoritative, but the profiles do not show fully autonomous downstream actions by default. The risk exists in default tool-enabled workflows, though verification can interrupt it.
conditions: IF open-webui uses Cline-generated text as a source for prompts, summaries, or tool calls without verification, errors can cascade.
IF either agent is configured to auto-act on the other’s output, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require human review before tool execution.
Mark inter-agent outputs as untrusted.
Add citation checks for factual claims.
Limit open-webui tool permissions during handoff.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles source code and browser screenshots, while open-webui handles prompts, documents, files, API keys, and usage analytics. Their documented storage and egress surfaces differ, so the same data class can be retained or transmitted under different policies. The profiles do not prove a residency breach, but they do show a compliance-mismatch pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into both agents, retention and logging differences can create policy mismatch.
IF open-webui sends content to external APIs while Cline keeps it local, residency or DPA obligations may diverge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared sessions.
Disable analytics and external connectors for sensitive runs.
Use region-locked providers only.
Document retention settings for both agents.
requires-engineering: align data-processing agreements and retention controls.
